Choose a source playlist and a target.
Songport ships without service keys. Create your own free key on the service\'s developer page: it takes about two minutes and the app guides you step by step.
Requires a Spotify account. Playlists and Liked Songs.

YouTube Music playlists and likes through the free companion app "Songport YTM Bridge" (installed separately, not from Google Play). No Google Cloud project, no quota. Not an official Google API: read the notice in the Bridge before using it.
Install the companion app "Songport YTM Bridge" from GitHub, then come back here and press Connect. Prefer the official route? Use the "YouTube Music (Google API)" card below.

Official YouTube Data API with a Google Cloud project of your own. Optional: the plain "YouTube Music" card above works without it. Daily quota is limited: large syncs may take several days.

Songport follows the system language: English, Italian, French, German.

Songport ships without keys of its own: Spotify, YouTube Music, TIDAL, Deezer, Last.fm and Apple Music connect through a free key created in your name, so their limits and quotas are yours alone. Here you can see and change them.
Songport is free with no subscriptions. It is supported by a single small banner ad; no data is sold and nothing leaves your phone except the requests to the music services you connect.
File playlists live inside the app. Import a file here, then use it as a sync source; or sync any playlist into a file and export it as CSV or M3U.
Saved inside Songport: use “Save as file” here, or Options → Files, to get a CSV or M3U.

Apple Music playlists in your library. Needs a subscription and a MusicKit developer token. Apple\'s API can add tracks but not remove them.

Local files: import a playlist you exported from any service (CSV, M3U, Apple Music/iTunes XML, JSON, or a plain list) and sync it anywhere. The bridge for services with no open API: Amazon Music, Qobuz, SoundCloud.

Spotify requires an app registered in your name. It is free; an app in Development Mode serves up to 5 accounts, plenty for personal use.
Google requires a Cloud project in your name to use the YouTube API. It is free and the daily quota is yours alone.
TIDAL requires an app registered in your name. It is free.
Deezer needs an app registered in your name. The https redirect page is provided by the project.
The developer token belongs to your Apple Developer account and expires after six months at most.
%1$s only allows a handful of users per app. Set up your own credentials: it is free and takes about two minutes.

Save any playlist of this service as a file on your phone, without changing anything on the service.

Finds tracks that appear twice in a playlist, even with a different ID or version, and keeps the first copy.
Some phones (Xiaomi, Huawei, Oppo, Samsung) stop background apps. Exclude Songport from battery optimisation so the schedule is respected.
Link received: choose where to sync it.

Your own music server: Navidrome, Airsonic, Gonic, LMS, Funkwhale and anything speaking the Subsonic API. No registration, no quota. Starred songs count as liked songs.
Your Jellyfin server. No registration, no quota. Favourites count as liked songs.
Your Plex Media Server, with your X-Plex-Token. Plex cannot create an empty playlist from the API: create it in Plex, then pick it here.
Loved tracks of a Last.fm profile, as a source only. Needs a free Last.fm API key.
Playlists and loved tracks of a ListenBrainz user, as a source only. No key needed.
Your credentials stay encrypted on this phone. Songport only talks to the server you enter here.

Enter the address of your Navidrome, Airsonic or other Subsonic-compatible server (for example https://music.example.com), your username and password. The password is never sent as-is: each request uses a salted hash.
Enter the address of your Jellyfin server (for example https://jellyfin.example.com), your username and password.

Enter the address of your Plex Media Server (for example http://192.168.1.10:32400) and your X-Plex-Token. Plex explains how to find the token in its support pages ("Finding an authentication token").
Enter the Last.fm username whose loved tracks you want to read. The profile must be public.
Enter the ListenBrainz username whose playlists and loved tracks you want to read.
Last.fm needs a free API key, issued instantly, to read public profiles.
%1$s is read-only: it can only be a source.
%1$s cannot create playlists from the app: create it in %1$s and pick it here.
You will sign in on %1$s, in your browser. Songport never sees your password.
You will sign in with your Apple ID in Apple\'s own window. Songport never sees your password.
Your server details stay encrypted on this phone. Songport only talks to your server.
Songport only receives a limited, revocable permission, stored encrypted on this phone (Android Keystore).
There is no Songport server: data travels only between this phone and %1$s.
You can revoke at any time: here with Disconnect, or from your %1$s account.
Delete the syncs using this account first.
Tap + to add a service: Spotify, YouTube Music, TIDAL, files… You can add several connectors of the same service, each with its own name and account.
The browser may already be signed in to another %1$s account. On the sign-in page choose “Not you?” or switch account, then continue with the account for this connector.

Experimental, via the Songport Bridge companion app. Amazon has no open API: the Bridge uses the web player\'s interface. Search and reading playlists work; library listing and writing are still being completed.
Install or update the companion app \"Songport Bridge\" (1.1 or newer) from GitHub, then come back here and tap Connect.
Passwords are typed on the services\' own pages, never in Songport.
Songport keeps only revocable access tokens, encrypted with the Android Keystore.
There is no Songport server and no account to create: nothing leaves your phone except requests to the services you connect.
Disconnecting deletes the token from the phone; every service also lets you revoke it from your account page.
Fingerprint, face or phone PIN before Songport opens.

Daily limit set by YouTube (Google), not by Songport. Resets at midnight Pacific time. A search costs 100 units, adding a track 50.
Daily limit set by YouTube (Google), not by Songport, shared by everyone using the built-in key: what other users consume is not counted here. Your own credentials give you a quota of your own.

Also creates the mirror sync in the opposite direction, without removals, so both playlists stay complete.
Available with an existing target playlist and a writable source.
Keep your playlists identical across music services, by hand or on a schedule. Free, no subscription, no account to create.
Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube Music, TIDAL, Deezer, your own server, or a file.
Pick a source playlist and a target. Preview shows exactly what will change before anything happens.
Every hour, day or week. Tracks that cannot be matched are listed so you can fix them yourself.
You sign in on each service\'s own page. Songport keeps only an encrypted, revocable token on this phone and has no server of its own.

Songport ships without service keys of its own: for Spotify, YouTube Music, TIDAL and Deezer you create a free key on the service\'s developer page, and the app walks you through it in about two minutes. Your data then flows only between your phone and your own key.
One track per line, as "Artist - Title". Numbers at the start of lines are ignored.

string-array.name: setup_steps_spotify
string-array.item: Sign in at developer.spotify.com with the Spotify account you use every day. Spotify requires that account to have Premium; if you are asked to accept the developer terms, accept them.
Press "Create app". Name and description are up to you (for example "Songport"). Leave "Website" empty.
In "Redirect URIs" paste exactly the address shown below and press "Add". Without it the login cannot come back to the app.
Under "Which API/SDKs are you planning to use?" tick "Web API", accept the terms and press "Save".
Open the app you created, press "Settings" (top right) and copy the "Client ID" here. You do not need the Client secret.
Optional: "User Management" lets you add up to 5 other Spotify accounts (name and e-mail) that may use your key, for example family members.

string-array.name: setup_steps_youtube
string-array.item: Sign in to console.cloud.google.com with your Google account and create a project. Any name works, for example "Songport". Wait for the notification that it has been created, then select it.
Enable the YouTube Data API v3: the link opens its page in the library, press "Enable".
Google Auth Platform, "Overview", press "Get started": app name "Songport", your e-mail as support address, audience "External", your e-mail as contact. Accept and press "Create".
Google Auth Platform, "Audience": under "Test users" press "Add users" and add your own Gmail address, then Save. Without this step Google refuses the login with "access blocked".

Google Auth Platform, "Clients", "Create client": application type "Desktop app", any name. Copy the Client ID and the Client secret here. Nothing else to register: the app receives the login on 127.0.0.1.

string-array.name: setup_steps_tidal
string-array.item: Sign in at developer.tidal.com with your TIDAL account.
Press "Create new app". Name and description are up to you.
In "Redirect URIs" paste exactly the address shown below and save.
Copy the Client ID here. The Client secret is not needed.

string-array.name: setup_steps_deezer
string-array.item: Sign in at developers.deezer.com with your Deezer account and open "My Apps".
Press "Create a new Application". Name and description are up to you.

Deezer only accepts https redirects. A ready-made redirect page is already filled in below: paste that address both in "Application domain" (without https://) and in "Redirect URL after authentication".
Save, then copy the "Application ID" here.

string-array.name: setup_steps_apple
string-array.item: Apple Music needs a paid Apple Developer Program membership (99 $ per year) and an Apple Music subscription. Without it, use public playlist links or files.
In "Certificates, Identifiers & Profiles", "Identifiers", create a Media ID with MusicKit enabled.

In "Keys" create a key with "Media Services (MusicKit)" enabled and download the .p8 file (it can be downloaded once). Note the Key ID shown next to it and your Team ID (top right of the account page).
Generate the ES256 developer token (JWT) from the .p8 key: the project README has a ready-made script. Paste the token here.
The token expires after at most six months: when the login stops working, generate a new one and paste it again.

string-array.name: setup_steps_lastfm
string-array.item: Sign in at last.fm and open the API account creation page.
Fill in the form: contact e-mail, application name and description are up to you. "Callback URL" and "Application homepage" can stay empty. Submit.
Copy the "API key" here. The "Shared secret" is not needed.

resources.string: Connect a music service, then create your first sync. It takes a minute.
Tap "New sync": pick a source playlist and where it should go.
Every sync leaves a report here: what was added, removed or not found.
Backup and duplicate cleanup work on the services you have connected.
You log in on each service\'s official page. Songport never sees your password.

Songport is free, with no subscriptions and no locked features. One small banner, never full-screen, pays for the developer\'s coffee and the hours spent keeping every service working. If it ever bothers you, open an issue on GitHub.
If you feel like it, buy the developer a coffee on Ko-fi. Totally optional: nothing is unlocked, the app stays complete for everyone.
